experiments.name: address-bypass pointer chase
experiments.notes: The stored experiment is the direct address chase (4 cycles). The second case puts add.d in the address path and measures 5, the general load latency. A third check, fld.d -> fadd.d -> movfr2gr.d -> address, gives the same 4 cycles for the data path, so the extra cycle belongs to the address path, not to the data path.

latencies.notes: 3 cycles of helper latency are subtracted. Unroll 10000, iters 1000. Raw measurement was 3.99; the residual is a systematic calibration offset, so the recorded value is the nominal integer with the observed spread.

cases.name: load result feeds the next address directly
load result passes through add.d before the next address

experiment.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 800 --unroll2 1600 --iters 40 --warmup 10 --reps 5 --init 'addi.d $r13, $sp, -1016; st.d $r13, $r13, 0; addi.d $r4, $r13, 0; li.d $r5, 0' --asm 'fld.d $f0, $r4, 0; movfr2gr.d $r4, $f0; add.d $r4, $r4, $r5'

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 5 --core 0 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024' --asm 'fld.d $f0, $r20, 0; fld.d $f1, $r20, 8; fld.d $f2, $r20, 16; fld.d $f3, $r20, 24; fld.d $f4, $r20, 32; fld.d $f5, $r20, 40; fld.d $f6, $r20, 48; fld.d $f7, $r20, 56'

notes: L1D-hit floating-point load. Two address paths, the same 4/5 split as ld.d: 4 cycles when the loaded value becomes the next address directly (bypass, the pointer chase) and 5 cycles when an ALU operation sits between the load result and the address. Both are measured through movfr2gr.d, which closes the loop back into the address, so the recorded cycles subtract its 3 cycles. Re-measured on LA464 and reproduced: the direct chase reads 6.90-6.98 cycles and 8.94-8.98 with add.d added, so the ALU form costs 2 more, not 1 -- one cycle is the add.d itself (a movfr2gr.d result feeding an add.d costs exactly 1.00 in a dedicated control) and one is the consumer penalty, the same penalty that makes an integer load 4 cycles on the AGU path and 5 through an ALU (ld.d chases at 3.94 and 5.97 with an add.d). A second, independent closure agrees: with fst.d and a reload closing the loop, fld.d -> fst.d -> ld.d reads 14.08 against 13.72 for a movgr2fr.d-sourced store behind an fadd.d, a difference of 3.34 that with the 1-cycle movgr2fr.d leaves ~4.3 cycles for the load. Do not use the plain movgr2fr.d -> fst.d -> ld.d control: a store whose data comes straight from a GPR bypasses the floating-point register file, and adding fadd.d to that chain costs 7 cycles instead of 3. The split 4 + 3 is a decomposition, not an independent measurement: only the sum of movgr2fr.d and movfr2gr.d (3.98 cycles) is directly measurable, so an assumed 2-cycle move would make the load 5. Measured with --method slope, unroll 800/1600, on LA464 core 0.
